topic: Certified-accuracy fixed-row spectral distributional-discrepancy benchmarks for unequal randomization. For fixed r>=2, integer B in Z^(r x n), rational prescribed treatment probabilities p_i, z in {-1,1}^n with E[z]=2p-1, and OPT=min_D lambda_max(E[B(z-Ez)(z-Ez)'B']), prove exact equivalence between assignment laws and reachable vector-prefix flows preserving every marginal and the terminal covariance. Construct rational epsilon-instance-optimal designs with matching PSD/spectral-Bellman lower certificates in time polynomial in the expanded lattice, input length, and log(1/epsilon); verify supplied algebraic exact certificates, claiming polynomial exact construction only when a polynomial-size projected covariance-hull description is supplied. Extract an optimal sparse law with at most n+r(r+1)/2 atoms, state the sharper attainable-feature-rank bound, preserve the corrected finite-population Horvitz--Thompson factor 1/(4n^2), and build a thin-matrix adapter/benchmark protocol for Rao--Zhang's released pure-balance MWU code. Explicitly credit Altschuler--Boix-Adsera for scalarized structured MOT, Haus for mixability/PARTITION, and standard SDP/ellipsoid machinery; exclude unrestricted exact construction, identity-block robustness, fixed counts, entropy constraints, superpopulation inference, and unexecuted performance claims. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Three fresh presolves derived exact flow/law and covariance preservation, minimax certificates valid at eigenvalue ties, explicit primal and spectral/Bellman feasibility repairs, a polynomial-bit dual box, covariance-preserving support compression, and exact marginal postprocessing for empirical MWU outputs. Exact symbolic checks verified the irrational optimum (67+sqrt(1609))/288 for a rational two-row unequal-margin instance; sixteen flow/Bellman/feature-rank cases and sixty marginal-repair cases passed. Boundary audits covered zero columns, rank deficiency, zero covariance, endpoint propensities, rational-value failure, support off-by-one errors, HT normalization, and projected-hull complexity; current-source checks found no complete-package collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Instantiate a concrete rational ellipsoid/truncation theorem and prove that the implementation meets the draft's exact-affine, delta-residual output contract in polynomial expanded-lattice, input-bit, and logarithmic-accuracy time; the conditioning bounds and repair algebra are supplied. EARLY KILL TEST: Execute the four-cell pilot: the irrational witness at certified gap <=2^-12, zero-column marginal preservation, a nondegenerate thin full-row-rank instance through unchanged-source zero padding, and the exact zero-matrix branch; independently verify repaired laws and certificates, stopping or pivoting if any mathematical cell fails or no nondegenerate consumer cell works without substantive source changes. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_fixedrow_ddm_spectral_certificate.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed row dimension r, determine whether unequal-probability spectral DDM admits an exact prefix-flow representation and a rational, certificate-producing epsilon-instance-optimal algorithm polynomial in the expanded lattice, input bit length, and log(1/epsilon), while retaining every prescribed marginal exactly.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves unrestricted constant-additive DDM hardness and gives an unequal-probability MWU guarantee polynomial in 1/epsilon rather than certified instance-optimal log(1/epsilon) complexity.
source_refs.author: Anup B. Rao and Peng Zhang

source_refs.claim: Structured multimarginal transport reduces certain fixed-marginal problems to dual-feasibility oracles and recovers exact sparse couplings for structured linear costs.
source_refs.author: Jason M. Altschuler and Enric Boix-Adserà

source_refs.claim: Fixed-row mixability instances admit pseudopolynomial dynamic programming despite strong NP-completeness in the unrestricted setting.
source_refs.author: Utz-Uwe Haus

source_refs.claim: Rational bounded SDP approximation has polynomial input-bit and log(1/epsilon) complexity when explicit radius and feasibility conditions are supplied.
source_refs.author: John Watrous

source_refs.excerpt: No positivity of a coordinate of p, of d_n(p), or of an observation probability was used.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior finite-orbit construction relies on permutation symmetry to collapse assignments to histogram cells and scalar risks; heterogeneous unit marginals destroy that reduction, while the spectral loss retains a full covariance matrix and is nonsmooth at eigenvalue ties. Rao–Zhang supplies unequal-margin DDM but not an instance-optimal logarithmic-accuracy algorithm or exact algebraic certificate. Haus covers a scalar fixed-row lattice problem, Altschuler–Boix-Adserà covers linear structured-MOT costs, and generic SDP bit-complexity does not automatically construct a rational coupling satisfying all affine marginals exactly. The first changed proof step is to replace orbit weights by a layered vector-prefix-flow polytope and combine its terminal covariance labels with PSD scalarization, an explicit bounded dual region, exact-affine repair, and rational primal recovery.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact assignment-law/prefix-flow equivalence and an algorithm returning a rational law D_epsilon plus rational PSD and Bellman certificates with E_D[z]=2p-1 and lambda_max(Cov_D(Bz))<=OPT+epsilon in time polynomial in the expanded lattice, input bits, and log(1/epsilon), together with a polynomial-time exact verifier.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest arc from unequal allocation to a distribution-over-assignments spectral objective and separates general hardness from constructive guarantees.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unequal assignment probabilities matter -> equal-probability balancing can be far from the unequal-margin optimum -> unrestricted DDM is hard -> fixed row dimension may permit certified expanded-lattice instance optimality

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the dual-feasibility-oracle and ellipsoid/column-generation proof for fixed-marginal couplings, replacing one linear terminal cost by PSD spectral scalarization and prefix-state dynamic programming.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A prescribed-marginal assignment law is a discrete multimarginal coupling, and the desired theorem likewise needs implicit exponential support, exact marginals, separation, and sparse primal recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the fixed-number-of-rows pseudopolynomial dynamic-programming proof, replacing scalar attainable row sums by vector prefix states and terminal covariance features.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems optimize dependence among finitely supported coordinates, with fixed output dimension making expanded-lattice state enumeration possible.

method_exemplars.technique: Instantiate rational ellipsoid approximation with explicit primal and dual radii, an exact-affine projection, and a rational eigenvalue-separation contract.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested logarithmic accuracy dependence and independently checkable spectral bounds require a concrete Turing-model SDP bit-complexity argument.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish finite-population inference for unequal-margin certified spectral-DDM laws by identifying conditions under which the correctly normalized Horvitz–Thompson estimator has a valid limit law, while determining whether independent repeated design waves can recover its randomization-induced covariance.

source_refs.claim: The unequal-probability design is analyzed through variance and MSE, but the paper does not provide a CLT or consistent variance estimator for the resulting dependent design.
source_refs.author: Anup B. Rao and Peng Zhang

source_refs.claim: A CLT for randomized-pivot Gram–Schmidt walk uses a skeletal martingale approximation and exchangeable-pair concentration tied to that algorithm's path.
source_refs.author: Sabyasachi Chatterjee, Partha S. Dey, and Subhajit Goswami

source_refs.claim: Rerandomization can produce a Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian limit, demonstrating that aggressive balance may change randomization asymptotics qualitatively.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.excerpt: Conditional independence of the two assignment waves therefore gives conditional independence
both assignment-coordinate families have the independence required by the cited theorem

open_problems.why_unsolved: A small terminal spectral covariance and exact marginal preservation determine the Horvitz–Thompson MSE but imply neither a Lindeberg condition nor a martingale representation. The Gram–Schmidt-walk CLT exploits a specific randomized-pivot trajectory, whereas a certified optimizer may return a sparse law supported on a few globally dependent assignments. The prior two-wave factorization plausibly survives dependence within each wave, but its concentration proof separately assumes coordinate independence. Thus its first changed step is the product-coordinate bounded-difference argument, which must be replaced by a flow-conditioned martingale, exchangeable-pair, or explicit joint-inclusion-probability argument; rerandomization results show that a non-Gaussian counterexample is also plausible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact cross-wave moment identity and a finite-population theorem giving verifiable conditions on certified unequal-margin DDM laws under which the Horvitz–Thompson estimator, with factor 1/(4n^2), has an explicit asymptotic variance, a CLT, and a consistent conservative variance estimator, plus a regime-specific non-Gaussian counterexample if those conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its unequal-allocation motivation and covariance-to-MSE bridge frame why a computationally certified design still needs its own inferential theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unequal allocation changes covariance and inverse-probability weights -> DDM controls worst-case MSE -> MSE control alone does not justify confidence intervals -> characterize when certified dependent designs permit valid finite-population inference

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the skeletal-process approximation, martingale CLT, and exchangeable-pair concentration, or isolate the precise step that fails without a Gram–Schmidt pivot path.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It obtains a precise Horvitz–Thompson limit law for the nearest spectral-discrepancy design but depends on algorithmic structure absent from a generic sparse optimum.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the covariance-to-HT-MSE identity, tail control, conservative variance construction, and design-based CLT while retaining unequal inverse-probability weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the canonical bridge from spectral balance to causal estimation and coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the projection decomposition into balanced and residual outcome components to detect discrete or truncated limit components generated by concentrated optimal laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how dependence introduced by a neighboring balance design changes the estimator's limiting distribution.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a rank-sensitive polynomial-time support-compression theorem for unequal-margin spectral-DDM laws that preserves every marginal and the full terminal covariance while attaining the n+r(r+1)/2 bound and its sharper attainable-feature-rank analogue.

source_refs.claim: The method optimizes over fixed-marginal assignment distributions but returns a sampler rather than a minimal explicit rational support preserving the full covariance.
source_refs.author: Anup B. Rao and Peng Zhang

source_refs.claim: The structured-MOT ellipsoid method recovers sparse vertex couplings but treats marginal constraints and a linear cost rather than added covariance moments.
source_refs.author: Jason M. Altschuler and Enric Boix-Adserà

source_refs.excerpt: This completes the finite positive-support saddle characterization without imposing overlap

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior construction characterizes which orbit cells may receive positive saddle mass but does not bound how many are necessary. Ordinary Carathéodory or transport-polytope sparsity does not directly provide a constructive bound after fixing n unequal first moments and every attainable symmetric covariance coordinate. Zero columns, endpoint propensities, rank-deficient B, and affine relations among reachable covariance features can lower the effective dimension, which must be computed on the attainable face rather than counted ambiently. The elimination must also retain rational weights, exact equalities, and polynomial bit length without an affine-rank off-by-one error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive elimination theorem transforming any rational feasible DDM law into an objective-equivalent rational law supported on at most n+r(r+1)/2 assignments, and more sharply affdim({(z,vech(B(z-Ez)(z-Ez)'B'))})+1 assignments, with exact moment preservation and polynomial bit-complexity bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the distribution over assignments as the operative design object, making explicit sparse realizability and auditability natural implementation questions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DDM chooses a joint assignment law -> implicit samplers obscure the law and its auditability -> only first and second assignment features determine the objective -> compress those features into an exact sparse design

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt vertex recovery and affine-dependence elimination by augmenting each assignment column with marginal and symmetric covariance features and computing rank in the attainable feature span.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both results convert an exponentially supported fixed-marginal coupling into an explicit sparse rational law while preserving all load-bearing linear statistics.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the independent unequal-propensity Bernoulli law attains the unrestricted fixed-row spectral-DDM optimum, including endpoint propensities, null assignment cells, and tied largest eigenvalues.

source_refs.excerpt: the common-probability independent designs form a subclass of the unrestricted designs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source proves a scalar independence frontier through a primal–dual risk sandwich and positive-support complementarity. With heterogeneous propensities, the product law is fixed rather than indexed by a common-probability simplex, while optimality is matrix-valued and must hold against a least-favorable PSD direction, including an eigenspace-valued subgradient when the top eigenvalue is tied. The first changed proof step is the scalar equality chain, which must become a trace pairing between a PSD spectral witness and covariance slack while retaining the source's zero-face logic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient PSD complementarity system, valid at eigenvalue ties and propensity endpoints, whose feasibility is equivalent to independent unequal Bernoulli assignment being spectrally optimal among all assignment laws with the same marginals.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing starts from ordinary randomization, isolates precision loss from imbalance, and asks what restricting the assignment law buys.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Independent randomization is causally valid -> realized imbalance reduces precision -> dependent assignment may improve balance -> locate the exact boundary where dependence cannot improve the spectral objective

method_exemplars.technique: Use minimax duality over balance directions and complementary slackness to compare a candidate randomization law with the unrestricted optimum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required object is an exact optimality certificate for a causal design under a worst-direction imbalance loss.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop and prove a source-preserving thin-matrix adapter and certificate-aware benchmark protocol for Rao–Zhang's released unequal-probability MWU implementation, covering zero columns, rank deficiency, a nondegenerate thin full-row-rank instance, and the exact zero-matrix branch.

source_refs.claim: The published experiments evaluate sampled operator-norm covariance and ATE MSE, perturb real covariates to obtain full row rank, and provide a floating-point Julia MWU implementation.
source_refs.author: Anup B. Rao and Peng Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Monte Carlo covariance estimates and floating-point eigendecompositions do not provide exact marginal or terminal-covariance auditing, while perturbing B to enforce full row rank changes the instance rather than proving invariance. A valid adapter must show that zero padding conjugates every relevant oracle update and preserves the assignment law and nonzero spectrum. The benchmark must then separate sampling error from optimization error using independently verified primal and lower certificates; the scan found the implementation and its simulations but no certified thin-input adapter or benchmark suite.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A zero-padding and row-space invariance theorem for the released MWU trace oracle, plus a reproducible checker that verifies exact supplied marginals and covariance, reports a certified primal–dual spectral gap, and executes the irrational, zero-column, nondegenerate thin, and zero-matrix cells without substantive source changes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its experiments and public implementation provide the natural baseline, performance quantities, and practical motivation for certificate-aware evaluation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: MWU improves empirical DDM objectives -> current evaluation uses sampled covariance and rank-enforcing perturbations -> thin and degenerate fixed-row instances require unchanged-instance handling -> add a proven adapter and independently certified benchmark

method_exemplars.technique: Mirror the matrix-MWU trace scalarization and prove conjugacy of every SVD, nullspace, and random-walk update under an isometric zero-row embedding, then audit output moments against exact certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The opportunity is specifically an invariant interface to this implementation, so its oracle construction and internal proof invariants are the load-bearing machinery.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether fixed-dimensional prefix-flow methods yield an online unequal-probability experimental design with exact conditional marginals and an instance-relative spectral-covariance guarantee against offline DDM, or prove an adversarial separation.

source_refs.claim: Online balanced experimental design allows arbitrary treatment probabilities but offers a worst-case logarithmic comparison rather than instance-optimality against each offline DDM instance.
source_refs.author: David Arbour, Drew Dimmery, Tung Mai, and Anup Rao

source_refs.claim: Optimal online vector discrepancy constructs sub-Gaussian signed distributions through tree prefix balancing and cloning, but treats symmetric signs rather than unequal causal-assignment marginals.
source_refs.author: Janardhan Kulkarni, Victor Reis, and Thomas Rothvoss

source_refs.claim: Unequal-probability DDM is an offline spectral covariance problem whose MWU construction uses the complete covariate matrix.
source_refs.author: Anup B. Rao and Peng Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing online work controls running weighted discrepancy and gives a worst-case MSE comparison, whereas offline spectral DDM sees all columns and minimizes the top eigenvalue of terminal covariance. The first changed step is the offline prefix-flow Bellman recursion, which must become a conditional covariance-to-go recursion over revealed states while enforcing each immediate treatment probability exactly. Tree prefix balancing constructs symmetric signed distributions, but targeted searches found no theorem combining unequal p_i, fixed r, online arrival, and a ratio or additive guarantee against the instance-specific offline spectral optimum.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an online policy theorem with Pr(z_i=1 conditional on the revealed covariate prefix)=p_i and lambda_max(Cov(Bz)) bounded by an explicit factor or additive term relative to offline fixed-r OPT, with a prefix Bellman certificate, or a matching adversarial lower-bound construction ruling out such a guarantee.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates sequential unit arrival, arbitrary treatment probabilities, causal MSE, and the cost of online decisions relative to offline balancing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Units arrive sequentially -> offline balancing cannot be executed -> weighted online discrepancy preserves arbitrary treatment probabilities -> ask whether fixed dimension permits instance-relative spectral performance or an impossibility boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt tree prefix balancing and cloning to distributions over unequal weighted signs, replacing symmetric cloning probabilities by exact propensity-preserving transitions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its output is already a distribution over online colorings with simultaneous prefix control, the structural ingredient needed for a randomized causal design.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over weighted online discrepancy, its ridge-regression comparison, and Horvitz–Thompson MSE analysis while replacing the worst-case potential by fixed-r spectral covariance-to-go.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats arbitrary-propensity online causal assignment and therefore supplies the estimator and exact-marginal layer.

method_exemplars.technique: Use matrix-MWU scalarization of lambda_max as the offline comparator and dual lower-bound mechanism.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired guarantee is explicitly relative to the unequal-margin spectral DDM optimum defined there.

literature_map:
Rao and Zhang (AISTATS 2025, arXiv:2411.02956) define the closest unequal-probability DDM problem, prove unrestricted constant-additive hardness, and give a polynomial-in-1/epsilon MWU design rather than certified instance optimality.
Harshaw, Sävje, Spielman, and Zhang (JASA 2024, arXiv:1911.03071) connect spectral balance, Horvitz–Thompson MSE, Gram–Schmidt walk construction, and design-based inference, primarily for symmetric allocation.
Chatterjee, Dey, and Goswami (Annals of Applied Probability 2025, arXiv:2305.12512) sharpen Gram–Schmidt-walk inference using a skeletal martingale and exchangeable-pair concentration tied to the walk's path.
Arbour, Dimmery, Mai, and Rao (ICML 2022, arXiv:2203.02025) handle online balancing with arbitrary probabilities but provide worst-case or logarithmic comparisons rather than instance-relative offline optimality.
Morgan and Rubin (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1207.5625) formalize rerandomization, while Li, Ding, and Rubin (PNAS 2018, arXiv:1604.00698) show its estimator may have a Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian limit.
Kallus (JRSSB 2018, arXiv:1312.0531) frames covariate balance as minimax experimental design and develops kernel allocation and worst-direction balance arguments.
Azriel, Krieger, and Kapelner (arXiv:2212.01887) contrast equal and unequal allocation under Neyman and population models, locating regimes favoring complete randomization or exact balance.
Davezies, Hollard, and Vergara Merino (arXiv:2407.13613) study unequal-probability balanced randomization via the cube method and derive Horvitz–Thompson and Hájek properties, with part of the asymptotic route conditional on a Poisson-approximation conjecture.
Altschuler and Boix-Adserà (Mathematical Programming 2023, arXiv:2008.03006) provide structured-MOT oracle reductions, exact marginal handling, ellipsoid recovery, and sparse couplings for structured linear costs.
Their companion hardness work (Discrete Optimization 2021, arXiv:2012.05398) shows that general multimarginal coupling optimization remains intractable without exploitable cost structure.
Haus (Operations Research Letters 2015, arXiv:1407.6475) connects complete mixability to multidimensional bottleneck assignment: general strong NP-hardness coexists with fixed-row pseudopolynomial dynamic programming.
Watrous (Theory of Computing 2009, arXiv:0901.4709) supplies a rational SDP/ellipsoid bit-complexity template and highlights the need for explicit radius and approximate-feasibility contracts.
Kulkarni, Reis, and Rothvoss (2023, arXiv:2308.01406) obtain online vector-discrepancy distributions through tree prefix balancing and cloning, but not unequal-margin causal instance optimality.
Recent nonlinear Gram-matrix balancing work occupies nonlinear Gram–Schmidt-walk extensions, but it does not close the fixed-row, exact-unequal-margin, certificate-producing spectral problem.
The scan found no complete collision combining fixed r, exact unequal marginals, rational epsilon-instance-optimality with log(1/epsilon) dependence, PSD/Bellman lower certificates, covariance-preserving compression, and an unchanged-source thin-MWU benchmark.
